correctness.rationale: All candidate solvency regimes are obtained by inverting the fixed 2x2 matrix; positivity of its inverse yields dominance of solvent configurations. The sign of F(c) is necessary and sufficient for high-bank solvency before the full-solvency threshold; exact sign at B/A gives critical beta. The four binary shock states exhaust the law, giving the expected default formula and slope. An independently executed bundled code checker returned 7,659 symbolic/exact-rational test assertions. Numerical tests are supplementary and are not used to prove global parameter claims.

value.rationale: A motivated systemic-risk question, whether shock dependence amplifies or relieves expected bank failures as reciprocal integration grows, receives an exact three-phase answer and a sharp distress-cost feasibility threshold. The transition persists for an explicit interval with positive book values, so it is not solely an artifact of negative equilibria. This is a structural parameter boundary, not an arbitrarily selected numerical experiment; no claim of empirical significance is made.
